clue.text: Mangled corpse heartlessly put out of view

indicators.note: something mangled is torn about and disfigured, so these letters are thrown into a new order
without its heart, the word put loses its middle letter and keeps only its first and last

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a mutilated body is quietly moved where nobody can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves PT from 'put'; 'Mangled' rearranges CORPSE with PT. 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide outlook or scene, the same sense as a view from a height.

clue.text: Europe set against taking in former currency

annotationWithheld.why: Europe set against taking in former currency (6): E (Europe) + SET fits inside P...A, but no clue word gives PA ('against' does not), so the wordplay cannot be completed honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Europe set against taking in former currency

clue.text: Big automobiles coveted by Hollywood types

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for big sizes
automobiles are cars

explanation.surface: Film people in Los Angeles love their oversized cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big automobiles' reads as one phrase about limousines, but 'Big' alone gives OS (outsize).
explanation.definitionFit: Academy Award statuettes are the prizes every film-industry figure in Hollywood longs to win.

clue.text: Late worker?

parts.note: late here means former rather than unpunctual or dead: someone who used to work and has now retired on an income

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' tempts you towards someone tardy or someone deceased; the sense is 'formerly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person drawing an income is, in a playful sense, a former employee.

clue.text: Socratic path could be disastrous

indicators.note: the letters of the two words could be rearranged into something else, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Following the questioning method of Socrates might lead to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SOCRATIC and PATH together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something catastrophic brings ruin on a huge scale, a direct synonym of disastrous.

clue.text: Setter is getting transport on foot

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says I am
a bus is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler takes the bus instead of walking.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to themselves as I or ME, so 'Setter is' gives I AM. 'getting' and 'on' are links; 'on foot' looks like walking, but 'foot' is metrical.
explanation.definitionFit: In verse a metrical foot of one short and one long syllable is this unit of prosody.

clue.text: Saw, say, a girl upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Here's an example: a young woman is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EG + ADA over to give ADAGE; ADA reads the same either way. 'Saw' is the noun meaning a proverb, not the tool or the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, an exact synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Bound like Buena Vista Social Club

parts.note: the Buena Vista Social Club was a group of musicians, that is a band
its Cuban players were mostly elderly, so they were old

explanation.surface: Tied up in the manner of a famous Cuban music group.
explanation.walkthrough: The Buena Vista Social Club was a celebrated group of veteran Cuban musicians who became famous late in life, so it was an old (BAND, AGED) group.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that has been bound up with dressings has been wrapped in strips of cloth.

clue.text: Radiation always sits around

indicators.note: the word sits goes around the other piece, placing it inside

parts.note: always means ever

explanation.surface: Background radiation is constantly present, sitting all around us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sits' looks like a verb about background radiation, but its letters are the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The sievert is the SI unit measuring the biological effect of a dose of radiation; the plural names an amount of it.

clue.text: Ill-written communication

parts.note: read not as badly written but as a message written because one is ill, excusing absence from work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-written' suggests poor handwriting; the hyphen hides 'written because of illness'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's certificate excusing absence from work is a message prompted by being unwell.

clue.text: Uncle from the new world?

definitions.meaning: uncle is slang for a pawnbroker, the person something is pawned to
of a Native American people of the Great Plains, so from the Americas

explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker; the person to whom goods are pawned is the pawnee. The Pawnee are also a Native American nation, hence the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally the pawnee is the party receiving a pledged item; separately, the Pawnee people are native to North America.

clue.text: Artist takes control of council

parts.note: to gain a place is to take control of it
a borough is a town with its own council, metonymically the council itself

explanation.surface: A painter seizes power over a local authority.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough is a famous English painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: What's astir? Broken bones

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of the neighbouring word are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the commotion is, and the reply is a set of fractures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges ASTIR. 'What's' is a link, and 'Broken bones' looks like an injury, but only 'bones' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the small bones of the ankle, plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Team least trained gets no satisfactory result

indicators.note: trained suggests being drilled into a new shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A poorly coached side ends up with a disappointing draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges TEAM and LEAST together; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock, where neither side can win, is an outcome that satisfies nobody, as in chess.

clue.text: En voyage without information and refusing accommodation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the travelling phrase surrounds the other piece

parts.note: en voyage, French for travelling, means in transit
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone travelling with no details declines to be put up anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: IN TRANSI(GEN)T. GEN is British slang for information. 'accommodation' means compromise, not lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigent people refuse to compromise or come to an accommodation with opponents.

clue.text: Odd sailing ship clears the drink

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the substance that clears drink

indicators.note: odd suggests something strange or out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: A strange vessel on the water cuts through the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges SAILING with SS. 'the drink' looks like the sea, but isinglass, a fish gelatin, is used to clear (fine) beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a gelatin from fish bladders used as a fining agent to clarify beer and wine.

clue.text: Girl taking time out faced the bowling, no less

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: taking a letter out removes it from the word

parts.note: in cricket, the batsman facing the bowling batted

explanation.surface: A girl took a break and went in to bat, no less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... out' removes T (time) from BATTED to leave BATED. 'no less' looks like an emphatic tag but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that continues without lessening keeps its full force, undiminished.

clue.text: Muck raised and pushed across to grating

indicators.note: the word sent spreads across the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: something sent has been pushed or propelled onward

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: muck is dirt

explanation.surface: Dirt is lifted and shoved over towards a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns DIRT upward into TRID, and 'across' sets SENT round it. 'grating' is the adjective, not the drain cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice is harsh and loud, the same as a grating sound.

clue.text: Lawyer for privatised trains?

parts.note: something privatised is no longer state-owned, i.e. not public
a railway is the trains; RY abbreviates railway, with A before it
the second half of the same phrase, not public

explanation.surface: A legal adviser is needed to handle the sell-off of the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'privatised trains' as NOT A RY PUBLIC: not a public railway. A notary public is a lawyer who certifies documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary public is an official, usually a solicitor, authorised to witness and certify documents.

clue.text: Blair or spring flower

parts.note: a spring is a well, a natural source of water

explanation.surface: A choice between a politician and a seasonal bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair, not Tony. 'flower' also defines: something that flows, the River Orwell in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Arthur Blair wrote under the pen name George Orwell.

clue.text: Old doctor curtailed food poisoning

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the final letters go

parts.note: listeria is a bacterium causing food poisoning

explanation.surface: A doctor of the past was cut off by a nasty stomach bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' removes IA from the end of LISTERIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was a Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery, a historical physician.

clue.text: Officer gets a rough ride from Yankee jail

parts.note: brig is American slang for a prison, especially on a ship or base

indicators.note: a rough version is crude and jumbled, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A military commander endures an uncomfortable trip away from an American prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges A and RIDE into ADIER. 'Yankee' is not Y here; it marks the jail word as American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Plant used for arbours?

parts.note: arbours are shady retreats or shelters; say a word for such shelters as a Cockney would, dropping its initial H, and it becomes a garden plant's name

explanation.walkthrough: Arbours are shelters; a dropped H, as in Cockney London speech, turns that word for shelters into the name of a rose-family plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Avens is a small perennial of the rose family, also called geum.

clue.text: Maxim of old Russian writer

parts.note: Maxim reads as a saying by the writer but is the first name of a Soviet-era novelist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maxim' looks like a proverb; it is the first name of the author of 'Mother'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxim Gorky, also spelt Gorki, was a Russian novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Old city falling short of ideal

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: the ideal thing is the best

explanation.surface: An ancient town did not live up to perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' drops the final T of THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was an ancient city in Egypt, and another in Greece.

clue.text: Capital finds flower in embryo a nuisance

parts.note: a bud is a flower not yet opened
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that an undeveloped bloom is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary.

clue.text: Dislike of French cricket?

parts.note: de is French for of
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the French hate cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a long international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to dislike intensely, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Painter takes game on plate to the queen

parts.note: whist is a card game
L is the learner plate shown on a British learner driver's car
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: An artist serves a dish of game to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like venison, but it is the card game WHIST; 'takes', 'on' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American-born painter based in London.
